children: to combine with Cayman Islands-based Bluechip & Co. Holdings.
The transaction values Bluechip at a Company Net Value of $400M, with Bluechip shareholders set to receive an aggregate of 40M Purchaser ordinary shares.
Flag Ship will merge into its newly formed subsidiary, Bluechip Holdings, which will survive as the publicly traded parent company.
Bluechip Merger Sub will then merge with Bluechip, making Bluechip a wholly owned subsidiary of the new public parent.

Flag Ship shareholders will receive one Purchaser ordinary share for each existing Flag Ship ordinary share, while existing rights will convert into Purchaser rights and ultimately be exchanged for one-tenth of a Purchaser ordinary share each.
Bluechip will fund certain Flag Ship transaction expenses through non-interest-bearing loans, which will be cancelled if the acquisition merger closes.
The combined company’s board is expected to have five directors, including nominees from Flag Ship and Bluechip and three directors expected to meet Nasdaq independence requirements.
Bluechip CEO Ming Zhang and its other officers are expected to become officers of the combined public company.
Bluechip’s businesses span insurance-related customer acquisition, financial education, referrals, U.S. capital-markets advisory, AI-driven online advertising and data-center services.

title: Flag Ship Acquisition announces $400M Bluechip business combination
